description: Participants treat every evaluation of an AI system as an experiment with a sampling design. On item-level results from small open-weight models on a fictional permits authority's synthetic bilingual task set, they compute clustered standard errors, compare systems with paired designs, size evaluations within a budget, use exact or Bayesian intervals for small sets, correct for grader error and audit benchmark claims. Graders and harnesses are built in AE-303, not here.
audience: Specialists. Data scientists who have completed the level 300 core or can show equivalent work: a defended analysis with a validated model or a causal estimate that they can explain.
prerequisites: DS-302 Online Experiments and A/B Testing
DS-305 Uncertainty, Interpretability and Model Validation
Computes bootstrap intervals and paired tests in code
Has logged a language model's outputs through an API

outcomes.text: Compute standard errors and intervals for an evaluation score that account for clustered items, repeated samples and small item counts, given item-level results where questions share source documents
outcomes.evidence: naive, clustered and small-sample intervals with design effects

outcomes.text: Decide whether the difference between two systems is real and large enough to matter, using a paired analysis, given item-level results for two configurations and a minimum effect
outcomes.evidence: a decision note with the paired difference, its interval and a verdict

outcomes.text: Design an evaluation's size in items, samples per item and grader calls to detect a stated difference within budget, given pilot variances and unit costs
outcomes.evidence: a sizing plan with power by formula, checked by simulation

outcomes.text: Evaluate the bias that grader error adds to a pass rate and correct it, carrying calibration uncertainty into the interval, given a model grader with 300 human-labelled verdicts in two languages
outcomes.evidence: corrected and uncorrected pass rates with intervals, by language

outcomes.text: Audit an evaluation claim for statistical validity, contamination risk and unequal tuning or token budgets, given a leaderboard-style report on four systems
outcomes.evidence: an audit memo classing each claim as supported, unsupported or untestable

outcomes.text: Design a reporting standard for evaluation claims, including results by language and subgroup, given the audit findings and a release process
outcomes.evidence: a two-page standard with required fields and a worked example
